tools.name: refresh_session
tools.description: Before session expiry, renew using the current Mcp-Session-Id. Save the returned header/token. A session is valid for 7 days; each refresh extends it by up to 7 days, never beyond a hard lifetime of thirty days from initialization; request and delivery expiries do not change.

tools.name: submit_requisition
tools.description: Request public web data as rows when browsing it yourself is impractical. Free sample first, one-off payment by the person, no signup or subscription. Collect every required field from the person first (sources, fields, filters, geo, row_target, deadline, language, description) and generate search_k

tools.name: get_request
tools.description: Read the current request, questions, sample and next action. After accepted payment, remind the customer about returned renewal/referral codes and expiry; pending codes are not ready. When next_action is wait, check again after suggested_check_after_seconds via a scheduled task if available; never l

tools.name: revise_requisition
tools.description: Revise an unpaid request using the current expected_revision with the full set of required fields. Existing samples and quotes are replaced. Use it when next_action is revise (including reason_code no_capability: try other sources or fields).

tools.name: confirm_scope
tools.description: Confirm the current immutable sample_id and revision and request a fixed quote. The quote is prepared asynchronously and emailed to the person with the payment link; check get_request on a schedule, never in a loop. After the final quote, use start_order or create_order to read the confirmation link

tools.name: confirm_quote
tools.description: Record final quote confirmation for quote_id and revision. Use start_order next; start_order also records this selection if not already confirmed.

tools.name: start_order
tools.description: Select the final quote and read the human confirmation link issued for the verified email (no second code). Save order_id and order_capability before passing confirmation_url to the person.

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Read or update the order for the final quote. Pass explicitly available renewal, referral or channel codes in coupon_codes before payment starts. tools.name: cancel_request
tools.description: Cancel an unpaid request and release unused coupons where payment has not started. Paid orders require support.

tools.description: Read the quote or estimated waiting time, without payment credentials.

tools.name: get_payment_status
tools.description: Check email verification, order creation and verified payment status. After payment, return this request’s coupon notifications and a separate delivery token when files are ready.

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Use the order_capability saved at order creation to read paid order status and obtain or renew a delivery token. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_email_verification, verify_email, start_order, create_order, get_payment_status, get_order · Private data: refresh_session, submit_requisition, confirm_quote, start_email_verification, get_quote, get_payment_status, get_order, fetch_delivery · Public sink: submit_requisition, start_email_verification, verify_email, start_order, create_order, get_payment_status, get_order, cancel_collection.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_email_verification, verify_email, start_order, create_order, get_payment_status, get_order · Private data: refresh_session, submit_requisition, confirm_quote, start_email_verification, get_quote, get_payment_status, get_order, fetch_delivery · Public sink: submit_requisition, start_email_verification, verify_email, start_order, create_order, get_payment_status, get_order, cancel_collection

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "fetch_delivery" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "After payment, use the delivery token to list files or read rows. Use json, csv, xlsx, fields.json, or rows pages; a paid excess-rows add-on has its own extra.json, extra.csv, extra.xlsx and extra.fields.json. XLSX is returned as base64 bytes with its content type. All rows pages for a file count on" → after: "After payment, use the delivery token to list files or read rows. findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
